summary: Adds an opt-in host-f64 post-processing operation that samples normalized analytic TE/TM electric-field component magnitudes at caller-supplied rectangular-guide cross-section points and reports the propagating-mode cutoff and beta.
selector: Set operation to cst-waveguide-electric-field-samples on module waveguide-modes; backend must be host (or omitted).
limitations: Closed-form, air-filled, perfectly conducting rectangular guide cross-section only; no dispersive or lossy materials, apertures, transitions, or full-wave solve.
Only propagating TE/TM modes with indices m,n in [0,15] are accepted; frequency must be in [1,1e15] Hz and guide dimensions in [1e-9,1e3] m.

Returns electric-field component magnitudes at 1 to 4096 in-bounds points; TE is normalized to peak Hz = 1 A/m and TM to peak Ez = 1 V/m, so values are normalized analytic fields rather than CST-calibrated results.
Host f64 only. An explicit CUDA/GPU/auto backend is rejected for this operation; no CST project, solver, port, or file compatibility is provided.
mappedFeature: Rectangular-guide electric-field cross-section sampling

summary: Adds an opt-in host-f64 operation that converts a caller-supplied complex impedance matrix into its scattering matrix by solving (Z + Z0 I) S = (Z - Z0 I), with bounded port count, shape and finite-value admission, and singular or ill-conditioned rejection.
selector: operation=cst-zmatrix-to-sparameters with module=zmatrix, backend=host, referenceImpedance, and zMatrix
limitations: Accepts 1 to 16 ports and one frequency-local complex impedance matrix per request.
Uses a single positive real reference impedance shared by every port; complex or per-port reference impedances are unsupported.
Input and output complex numbers use [real, imaginary] pairs; this is network postprocessing, not a field solver or CST project/API implementation.
Host f64 only; explicit CUDA requests are rejected. Singular or relatively ill-conditioned Z + Z0 I systems are rejected.
mappedFeature: Common-real-reference multiport Z-matrix to S-parameter conversion
